Zurishaddai
zoo-rih-SHAD-eye
proper noun
Hebrew Tsurishadday (H6701), my rock is the Almighty — from tsur (H6697), rock, and Shaddai (H7706), the Almighty.

Biblical Definition

Zurishaddai was a man of the tribe of Simeon in the generation of the exodus, and Scripture names him five times, always as the father of Shelumiel the prince of Simeon (Num 1:6; 2:12; 7:36, 41; 10:19). Like Shedeur of Reuben he has no recorded word or act of his own. What he has is a name that states a doctrine outright: my rock is the Almighty. Both halves matter. Tsur, rock, is the covenant title of God in the Song of Moses, where it is pressed six times over — He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment (Deu 32:4). Shaddai, the Almighty, is the name by which God made Himself known to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob before the name Jehovah was declared to Moses (Exo 6:3). So the name binds together the patriarchal revelation and the wilderness confession, and it puts them in the first person singular: not the Almighty is a rock, but my rock is the Almighty. That possessive is the difference between doctrine held and doctrine trusted. Father and son together confess the whole of it — the father, that the Almighty is his refuge; the son, that God is his peace. Refuge first, then peace: the order in which a soul actually receives them.

Origin & Era

A Simeonite of the exodus generation, father of Shelumiel prince of Simeon; his name means my rock is the Almighty.

ZURISHADDAI, Hebrew Tsurishadday, my rock is the Almighty.

A man of the tribe of Simeon in the generation that came out of Egypt.

Father of Shelumiel, prince and captain of the children of Simeon.

Named five times in the book of Numbers, always as the father of Shelumiel.

The name joins tsur, rock, to Shaddai, the Almighty.

Key Scripture

Num 1:6 — "Of Simeon; Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai."

Num 2:12 — "And those which pitch by him shall be the tribe of Simeon: and the captain of the children of Simeon shall be Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai."

Num 7:41 — "And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this was the offering of Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai."

Num 10:19 — "And over the host of the tribe of the children of Simeon was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai."

Modern Corruption

God as rock is softened into a figure for personal resilience; Scripture means an immovable Person outside the self.

expand to see more

The rock language of Scripture is regularly borrowed for a doctrine it contradicts — the idea that a man must find the bedrock within himself, that strength is discovered by looking inward and holding steady. Every biblical use points the other way. The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust (Psa 18:2). A rock is valuable precisely because it is not the man: it does not move when he moves, does not fail when he fails, and can be stood upon when he has no standing of his own. Zurishaddai's name locates the rock outside himself and above himself, and calls it Almighty.

The second recovery is the possessive. My rock is the Almighty. Scripture is full of men who knew the doctrine and perished for want of the pronoun; the wilderness generation heard the truth and it did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it (Heb 4:2). Sound theology held at arm's length saves nobody. What the name of a Simeonite father models is the personal appropriation the confessions call saving faith — not merely assenting that God is a rock, but resting the whole weight of one's soul on Him as mine.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Tsurishadday (H6701), from tsur (H6697), rock, and Shaddai (H7706), the Almighty — my rock is the Almighty.

expand to see more

Hebrew tsur (H6697) — a rock, cliff, stronghold; the Song of Moses calls the LORD the Rock six times over (Deu 32).

Hebrew Shaddai (H7706) — the Almighty; the name by which God appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Exo 6:3).

Hebrew Tsurishadday (H6701) — my rock is the Almighty; the Simeonite father of Shelumiel, Numbers 1:6, 2:12, 7:36, 7:41, 10:19.

Hebrew machseh (H4268) — a refuge, a shelter from storm; the companion idea to tsur throughout the Psalms.

Greek petra (G4073) — a rock, a mass of rock; that Rock was Christ (1Co 10:4), the wilderness confession answered in the Son.

Usage

"“Of Simeon; Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai”."

"“This was the offering of Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai”."

"“My rock is the Almighty” — a doctrine of refuge carried as a family name."
